newsitem.title: FRANCE: France to sell another five pct of Bull.
newsitem.headline: France to sell another five pct of Bull.

text.p: The French Finance and Industry ministries said in a statement the government planned to sell at least another five percent of computer maker Cie des Machines Bull, which would reduce its stake to below 50 percent.
The state now has 54 percent after placing stakes with NEC, Motorola, France Telecom and DNP.
It said interested investors had 15 days to make offers for 1,400,000 shares, about one percent of the capital. The price of the sale and the buyers will be decided by the Finance Ministry.
The sale will take place over the coming weeks under the control of the independent Privatisation Commission.
"Public sector ownership, held by the French state and France Telecom, will go below 50 percent, marking Bull's return to the private sector," Bull said in a statement.
Bull said it requested that its shares be suspended.

The operation will take the form of a capital increase that has yet to be determined and which will be subscribed by the state and other Bull shareholders. After the increase, the state will sell shares to private investors.
Bull currently has 137 million shares. The share closed at 33 francs on Tuesday, valuing the group at 4.5 billion.
A spokesman for Bull said the state would sell some seven percent -- or 316 million francs at Tuesday's share price.
France Telecom, currently state-owned but also slated for partial privatisation, has a 17 percent stake in Bull.
Japan's NEC and Motorola also have 17 percent, while Dai Nippon Printing (DNP) holds 3.3 percent. The state's direct stake is 36 percent. IBM Corp has 1.6 percent.
